paragraphs: Here's what I see, friend. Two men say they want to follow Jesus, and He doesn't sweet-talk either one. To the scribe He says, "Foxes have dens and birds of the air have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to lay His head" (Matthew 8:20). To the other disciple He says, "Follow Me, and let the dead bury their own dead" (Matthew 8:22). I think Jesus wants us to know what following Him looks like, and it comes before comfort, before plans and before our own list of firsts.

Then comes the boat, and the disciples got in because they followed Him (Matthew 8:23). Following Him didn't keep them out of the storm. They were right where He told them to go, and the waves still came. I've had days like that, where I did the right thing and the oven still caught fire. A storm doesn't mean you took a wrong turn.

And look who's in that boat with them. When they cry out, "Lord, save us! We are perishing!" (Matthew 8:25), He gets up and the sea is "perfectly calm" (Matthew 8:26). The men ask, "What kind of man is this? Even the winds and the sea obey Him!" (Matthew 8:27). So here's the big idea, baker: Jesus is worth following when it costs you, and He is worth crying out to when the waves are over the side. Follow Him, and bring Him the storm.
